page: Amazon Web Services c8gd.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro system and powered by 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 CPUs. It features 48 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.8 GHz without hyperthreading, alongside 96 GB of System RAM, providing a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio. The processor carries 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB shared L3 cache, with hardware support for AES encryption. Complementing the compute architecture is a bundled 2850 GB local NVMe SSD instance storage array and a baseline network bandwidth of 22 Gbps.

Benchmark testing reveals top-tier multi-core compute and memory bandwidth capabilities. The server excels in parallel execution, reaching a Geekbench multi-core score of 23,361 and a software compilation score of 69,900. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 381.77 GB/sec, while write bandwidth reaches 181.15 GB/sec, placing memory throughput in the highest benchmark bracket. High-concurrency operations show strong results, including 99.59 million Redis SET operations per second, 100.03 GB/sec static web serving throughput, and high PassMark database operation scores. Single-core performance across stress-ng and Geekbench remains in the middle category.

The instance offers favorable cost efficiency for multi-threaded, I/O-intensive compute workloads by pairing high-density ARM physical cores with fast direct-attached NVMe storage. Tradeoffs include a lower memory allocation of 2 GB per core, average single-threaded performance, and the absence of x86 vector extensions such as AVX-512 or dedicated GPU accelerators. The c8gd.12xlarge is best suited for parallel software compilation, high-throughput web serving, in-memory caching systems like Redis, and localized database workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gd.12xlarge is a compute-optimized ARM64 server powered by 48 dedicated physical cores of AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 running at 2.8 GHz. Managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance includes 96 GB of RAM (2 GB per core), 22 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, and a bundled 2850 GB local NVMe SSD. Benchmark data highlights top-tier multi-core performance and memory bandwidth, achieving 381.77 GB/sec uncached memory reads and high software compilation speeds. It demonstrates strong throughput in static web serving and Redis caching. Tradeoffs include an average single-core performance profile, a relatively low memory-to-core ratio, and the absence of discrete GPU hardware or x86 instruction sets. This instance delivers effective cost efficiency for parallelized build environments, web serving, and database workloads requiring low-latency local storage.
